changes.before: Implement accessDecision(session,allowed). Match the worked contract and the changed-input checks without modifying the supplied input values.
changes.after: Check who is signed in before checking what they may do.

before: Authentication establishes who is making a request. Authorization decides whether that identity may perform the requested action.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.
The first branch handles a missing trusted session. Only after an identity exists does the allowed decision matter. This helper does not create or validate session tokens.

Read the function call accessDecision(null, true) from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, accessDecision runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
A signed-in user lacks permission. Which result fits? Being signed in does not grant every permission. The identity is known, but this action is forbidden.
after: Authentication checks who is making a request. Authorization checks whether that person may perform this action. Knowing who someone is does not give them every permission.
A session represents a sign-in the server has already verified. This function receives that trusted session or a missing value, plus an allowed decision made by trusted code.
if (!session) detects the missing session in this model. Return sign-in before considering permission. The helper does not create or verify a session itself.
With a session present, return allow when allowed is true and forbid when it is false. A signed-in person can still be forbidden from performing this action.
Complete accessDecision(session, allowed). Keep the identity check first, then use the supplied permission decision. Do not change either input.

changes.before: Runs as a pure JavaScript function in the browser. Passing checks does not establish live HTTP behavior, database durability, concurrency safety, authentication security, queue delivery guarantees, or production readiness.
changes.after: This browser exercise models a decision. A real server must verify the session and determine permission itself, rather than trust caller-supplied claims.

project.title: Separate identity from permission
project.task: Complete accessDecision: missing session gives sign-in; otherwise allowed selects allow or forbid.
project.done_when: Identity is checked first, and signed-in callers still need permission.
